A lot has happened this past year, and if you've followed @keychain account posts, you know that we have continued building, improving, and expanding Hive Keychain across our mobile apps, browser extensions, and supporting infrastructure.

Let's start with some numbers to put Hive Keychain in perspective:

![5](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/S1QJCHNsZg.png)


For a detailed breakdown of how resources have been used, please refer to our transparency report:
👉 [Transparency Report](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@keychain/hive-keychain-dhf-and-transparency-update)

The current proposal is coming to an end, but there is still much we want to achieve to continue strengthening Hive’s ecosystem — which is why we are submitting this new proposal.

---

## Hive Keychain DHF

This new proposal will start immediately after the current one ends, with no overlap between the two.

Our vision remains unchanged and continues to focus on three main goals:

**Development**: Maintaining, improving, and expanding our extensions, mobile apps, and infrastructure based on user needs and ecosystem demand.

**Cooperation**: Working with dApps and services both inside and outside of our Hive ecosystem.

**Bridging Hive**: Expanding Hive’s reach through multichain integrations, starting with EVM (now in internal testing phase).

---

# I. Development

Developing and maintaining Hive Keychain products remains our core objective.

The following sections highlight both what has been achieved and what we aim to improve next across this full stack.

---

## 1/ Keychain Extension

Our extension remains at the forefront of development and continues to be the first platform to introduce new features. 

### Some highlights from this year:

* Introduced Keyless Mode for travelers, nomads or single use of a borrowed device
* Started the integration of several on/off ramp, swap and bridge providers for Hive and non-Hive cryptos
* Expanded anonymous request capabilities
* Introduced new requests and detailed history for operations such as savings and escrow transactions
* Added more information on the confirmation pages for better verification
* Improved RPC handling
* Improved the Hive Multisig integration
* Added Shortcuts to change account and navigate through the extension instantly
* Started internal testing  of the EVM  integration. More on this below (see 3/)
* Prepared a [key change and account recovery tool](https://recovery.hive-keychain.com)
* Continuous UX and performance improvements
* Implemented all new features introduced by the Hard Fork: extended multisig window, multiple recurrent transfers to the same user, new Voting Mana calculation

We also have a few features that have already been developed but will be shipped with EVM as they are used on both ecosystems:
* A proper contact list
* A standardized warning system
* Customizable push notifications   

### Next steps:

* Improve EVM UX based on our several rounds of testing. After the current internal round of testing, we will go through a closed Alpha, then an open Beta. More on this in section III/
* Keep enhancing our notifications system by making it more beginner-friendly
* Continue implementing community-requested features
* Add support for Hive-x402 for Hive native payments ([Read more](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@ecency/hive-joins-the-internet-native))
* Introduce our Gamification system (on both extension and mobile), to encourage user retention on Hive, by giving incentives to try different dApps. This is still in the ideation stage, but here are some ideas we have in mind:
    - Show users'stats with a leaderboard for each parameter.
    - Reward them for healthy, productive, or socially valuable actions with an XP system.
    - Display badges, levels, and progress bars inside Keychain.
    - Trigger optional shareables for social media or Hive posts.
    - Create campaigns with other dApps to promote all Hive dApps beyond our Ecosystem page. 
* Maintain compatibility with future Hive Hardforks
* Introduce new Partnerships and chain integrations
* Add Lite Account support when available
* Add a more streamlined Ticker Action page
* Add support for more hardware wallets
* Introduce an interactive Onboarding Guide for new users
* Users / Devs support
* More in the III/ Multichain section

---

## 2/ Keychain Mobile

Mobile continues to be one of our main focuses. It is now very close to full parity with the extension in terms of features, except, of course, for the coming EVM integration. On top of that, our in-App browser is now packed with new features which make your everyday mobile Hive experience even better!

### Some highlights from this year:

* Improved browser navigation through gestures
* Enhanced favorites & history Management (introduced reordering and deletion through gestures)
* Added the Dynamic Hive Engine RPC to avoid intrusive "Change RPC" popups
* Download Media and Find in Page browser features
* Ability to "Open", "Open in another tab", "Copy link", or "Share" a link after a long press in the browser
* Security updates and account management improvements
* Swap integrations and feature parity with extension
* Big refactor of the login now allows direct biometrics login rather than necessitating both the PIN and biometrics
* Browser navigation state is now preserved across restarts
* Added a way to change the login PIN code
* Performance and UX refinements
* Expanded anonymous request capabilities
* Introduced new requests and detailed history for operations such as savings and escrow transactions
* Added more information on the confirmation pages for better verification
* Implemented all new features introduced by the Hard Fork: extended multisig window, multiple recurrent transfers to the same user, and new Voting Mana calculation
* New languages added

### Next steps:

* Bring full EVM support to mobile. We made a clear separation between our EVM UI/UX and the utilities that can be shared between the extension and the mobile Apps. This will cut our development time drastically, although it will remain a huge endeavour.
* Continue improving browser usability
* Expand feature parity with extension
* Optimize performance and stability
* Introduce the gamification system
* Introduce an interactive Onboarding Guide for new users
* Add light accounts when they come out
* Enable NFC capabilities and integrate the Debit Card (we are currently waiting for the @hivedebit team to provide us their SDK)
* Introduce portfolio and ticker widgets for iOS
* Enable import of accounts through a .kc file, as is already possible on the extension side
* Implement OTA (over the air) updates on mobile so we can deliver faster updates directly in-App)
* Add support for Hive-x402 (see in 1/)
* Submit an appeal to Apple after they forced us to remove the 'Conversion' core chain feature from the App


---

## 3/ Keychain Swaps

Keychain Swap continues to play a central role in connecting tokens across Hive and beyond. This year, we improved safety and reliability (better price handling, failure cases, and routing) while integrating providers such as StealthEX and Changelly to open direct paths between Hive assets and the wider crypto ecosystem.

The next evolution is the introduction of a full aggregator experience inside Keychain. The first version will combine Portfolio, Buy, Sell, Swap, and Bridge into a single interface, powered by multiple providers (6 to start). This will allow users to seamlessly move between Hive, L2 tokens, and external chains while always getting the best route based on price and reliability.

Beyond UX, this is a key part of our business model: by aggregating liquidity and routing across providers, Keychain can begin generating sustainable revenue, helping reduce long-term dependency on DHF funding while continuing to deliver core infrastructure to the ecosystem.

We already started working on the Aggregator, and here is a sneak peek for you:

![](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/rJV8dNth-l.png)
![](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/S1EUuVt3-e.png)



### Next steps:

* Expand routing across multiple swap providers, aggregators, and bridges to provide the fastest and cheapest routes
* Integrate EVM-compatible assets
* Launch the full Aggregator 
* Improve rates, reliability, and execution efficiency across providers
* Improve and expand our Swap Widget capabilities to match our in-app Swap.

---

## 4/ SDK & Playground

Developer tooling remains a priority for easy access to all devs to our ecosystem and Hive. Making it easy to integrate Hive Keychain into any dapps is the fastest way to deploy any project on Hive, and for that, we:

* Revamped the Playground (Gitbook-style interface) 
* Expanded request support for savings and all escrow transactions (transfer, accept, reject, dispute)
* Improved documentation and testing tools


![](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/Bysm_vjhbg.png)



### Next steps:

* Continue improving developer onboarding processes 
* Expand SDK capabilities with EVM requests
* Support new request types and integrations (including EVM)
* Update our landing page with all the information about EVM integration and new partnerships
* Create a Keychain AI Skill to make it even easier to integrate Keychain

---

## 5/ Infrastructure & Backend

Our backend infrastructure has evolved significantly, especially with the introduction of multichain (EVM) support.

A key component of this is the development of a light node system, a heavy backend layer that continuously monitors addresses across supported chains. This is necessary in order to provide advanced features that are not readily available on public RPCs, while mitigating the costs of using third-party providers.

Supporting this level of functionality requires a robust and scalable infrastructure, with significant DevOps work to maintain uptime and performance while adding multiple third-party integrations to enrich data and capabilities

**This backend layer powers critical features such as:**
- Full transaction history across all chains
- Token and NFT discovery and metadata enrichment
- Smart contract interaction analysis
- Gas fee oracles and transaction gas estimation
- Cross-chain asset visibility

As Keychain evolves into a multichain wallet, this infrastructure becomes a core pillar of the product, ensuring a seamless and reliable experience for users across all supported ecosystems. 

---

## 6/ And much more

Over the past year, we have continued delivering features across all components of our stack, including several core projects that power our ecosystem. Beyond the extension, mobile apps, swaps, and SDK, our work also spans:

- **Keychain Store:** the easiest way for merchant payments + global map, powering 77 businesses (mostly in Venezuela) to accept HBD payments in their store 
- **Hive Multisig:** is now maintained by the Keychain team to provide multisig and 2FA on Hive [here](https://multisig.hive-keychain.com/)
- **Landing Page:** [hive-keychain.com](https://hive-keychain.com/) with a new look, more languages, and better SEO performance 
- **Keychain Commons:** shared utilities across projects
- **Tools:** [Hive QR Code generator](https://qr.hive-keychain.com/), [recovery tool](https://recovery.hive-keychain.com/), [our dashboard](https://dashboard.hive-keychain.com/) and more

---

# II. Cooperation

## 1/ On Hive

We continue working closely with projects across the Hive ecosystem:

* Supporting dApps with Keychain integration
* Adding new dApps to our Hive ecosystem screens, for easy dApp discovery on both extension and mobile
* Collaborating on onboarding and UX improvements
* Contributing to ecosystem-wide features (multisig, 2fa)
* Creating social campaigns with different dApps using our social channels

Future cooperations:
- implementing the Hive Debit Card as soon as their SDK is ready
- adding Hive-built swaps and bridges when production-ready (Magi swaps, wrapped HIVE, etc.)

## 2/ Outside of Hive

We are actively expanding Hive’s reach beyond its current ecosystem:

* Partnerships with swap providers and aggregators
* Discussions with external crypto companies and L1 blockchains
* Pushing for HIVE / HBD listing whenever possible

Some providers we've contacted already support Hive, while others are evaluating integration. These efforts aim to make Hive more accessible and connected globally. We're also looking into digital and physical debit card providers to see if there are some possibilities for Hive integration.

You can find more details about this topic in our latest [transparency report](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@keychain/hive-keychain-dhf-and-transparency-update).

---

# III. Multichain

Multichain integration has become a major focus of our work over the past year and represents a significant investment of time and resources from the team. Although this code hasn't been deployed to production yet, it can be found in the `feature/evm` branch that is currently 697 commits ahead of the `master` branch. We strongly believe this major update will be a game-changer for Hive, as it will enable the ecosystem to connect directly with the broader crypto landscape rather than operate in isolation.

EVM integration is not just about adding new chains; it is about bringing liquidity, users, and interoperability to Hive, while making it easier for developers from outside ecosystems to interact with Hive using familiar standards. 

We are currently in the internal testing phase of our EVM integration. This stage focuses on validating core flows, ensuring stability, and identifying edge cases before exposing the feature more broadly. Once we're satisfied with this, we will continue with a closed alpha testing phase with a few selected testers and finally, a wider open alpha, on which anyone will be able to participate.

We will actively look for testers willing to spend time using the product and providing meaningful feedback, as these testing phases will be critical to ensuring a solid transition to a multichain wallet.

![](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/Hyj-_Rjnbe.png)



Our first version aims to provide a full-fledged EVM wallet experience on 7 of the most popular EVM chains: Ethereum, Base, BSC, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche, and Arbitrum, as well as their testnets.

To list a few of the many features we've implemented:

- Account creation and management across selected EVM chains
- Automatic token and NFT discovery
- RPC handling
- Full history
- Account value
- Token and NFT transfers
- Contact list
- Automatically switch to the chain the current dApp is using
- Login and Transaction signing for EVM dApps
- Gas fee calculation
- Spam token/NFT detection
- ENS detection
- EVM Swaps
- Smart contract analysis
- Security warnings during dApp requests

![13](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/HJt5e53hbx.jpg)
![14](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/B1Kqe53nWx.jpg)
![15](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/rJYqxc22Zl.jpg)
![16](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/S1Fqg5hhWe.jpg)



Next steps:

- Improve EVM UX and stability based on testing feedback
- Expand supported features
- Add chain coverage 
- Bring EVM support to mobile
- Strengthen interoperability between Hive and EVM ecosystems
- Add onboarding funnels from EVM users to Hive

---

# IV. Additional Work

## 1/ Support

We continue to provide support through Discord and community channels, helping users and developers integrate and troubleshoot.

## 2/ Community Growth

We continue expanding Hive Keychain’s presence beyond Hive through social platforms (X, Linkedin) and partnerships.

## 3/ Infrastructure

We maintain and scale backend systems required to support our APIs, swaps, multisig, as well as our current multichain integration. 

---

# V. Budget

For this new proposal, we are reducing our budget to 540 HBD/day, a 10% decrease from our past proposal, in order to lower a bit our impact on the DHF. Our medium-term goal is to reduce further our proposal's budget once we have a stable income from our swap aggregation services.
This cut, along with a non-negligible increase in our infrastructure and API costs due to the multichain integration, will translate into a 24% cut of our development costs. This has been rendered possible by the rapid improvement of AI technology, which allows us to greatly increase our output while reducing the manpower involved. That being said, there are limits to this, especially for software as security-sensitive as a crypto wallet.
After these changes, our monthly budget will look as follows.

- Development (2 full-time senior devs, 1 part-time): $ 11,400
- CM & Ecosystem growth: $ 850

- Tools (others): $ 130

For more information about these different items, read our [transparency post](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@keychain/hive-keychain-dhf-and-transparency-update).

---

# VI. Commitments

* Keep our extensions, mobile apps, and main projects open-source
* Continue regular updates and transparency posts
* Deliver features aligned with the proposal scope
* Strive to generate more revenue through our swap features, in order to reduce our reliance on the DHF. Publish revenue publicly.
* Include Hive in any way possible in all marketing efforts and collaborations with new partners.

Take a look at the stance of this structure, which seems to be defying the passage of time. With its powerful and imposing presence, it appears to be holding onto the traces of the past as if they were a badge of honor. The weeds sprouting from between the walls, meanwhile, reveal the structure’s harmony with nature. The name of this ancient city I came across during my Aegean tour is known as the Ancient City of Kaunos. 

>Zamana direnmeye çalışan şu yapının duruşuna bir bakın.   Etrafına yaydığı güçlü ve gösterişli duruşuyla sanki geçmişin izlerini bir onur gibi hala ayakta tutabiliyor.  Duvarların aralarından çıkan otlar ise, yapının doğayla olan  barışıklığını gözler önüne seriyor. Ege turumda karşıma çıkan bu antik kentin adı Kaunos Antik Kent olarak biliniyor. 

[//]:# (!worldmappin 36.82597 lat 28.62206 long  d3scr)

![IMG20260325174049 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXidKHHZyPqtWAcFjt9yDkyva1ooEUuvpTFKaD9rYXts3/IMG20260325174049%20(1).jpg)


Köyceğiz, one of the stops on my Aegean tour, is among the most beautiful districts of Muğla Province. One of the best-known ancient cities near Köyceğiz is the Ancient City of Kaunos. Köyceğiz is known for the lake that surrounds it in an oval shape. The ancient city is located in the village of Çandır, to the west of the Dalyan River, which connects the lake to the Mediterranean coast. Our journey, which began around the quiet, serene, and still lake of Köyceğiz, took us through the water-laced paths of Dalyan until we reached the Ancient City of Kaunos. By then, we had realized that we were not merely visiting an ancient city but were also stepping into the depths of the past. 

>Ege turu rotalarımdan biri olan Köyceğiz, Muğla ilinin en güzel ilçeleri arasında yer alıyor. Köyceğiz'e en yakın en bilinen antik kentlerinden biri de Kaunos Antik Kenti'tir. Köyceğiz, etrafını oval şeklinde kaplayan gölü ile bilinir. Gölü Akdeniz kıyısına bağlayan ve yakınında bulunan Dalyan Çayı'nın batı yönündeki Çandır Köyünde Antik Kent yer almaktadır. Köyceğiz'in sessiz sakin ve durgun duran gölün etrafından başlayan yolculuğumuz,  Dalya'nın suyla iç içe  geçmiş yollarından geçerek Kaunos Antik Kenti'ne vardığımızda, sadece antik bir kent değil, geçmiş zamanın derinliklerine doğru da yürüyeceğimizin farkına varmıştık. 

![IMG20260325180608.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWBtxDRagjiQLVk9M8TMC2SjV3q87Pcre7VeSvfpBMHVi/IMG20260325180608.jpg)

![IMG20260325164220.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc1uLhirNUzgRZReqh2MEYXZ9wZZB8mPiVRJuyNi8ZMPL/IMG20260325164220.jpg)

![IMG20260325165837.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeVeGft6USjTjYUczSH3gTACbmvnZedzoEi4eTZEsWJG7/IMG20260325165837.jpg)

![IMG20260325173527.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXdYgsMTPtYvq3yeg5sug8YA2oRp2ywDoD7PdMpLBEfd8/IMG20260325173527.jpg)

You enter the city via a long, narrow path carefully paved with speckled stones. They probably charge an admission fee to tour the city, but since there was no one at the ticket booth, we went straight in. By the time we arrived, the rain had intensified. But this rain and the scent of the earth added a special charm to our visit. It was as if nature had awakened within the city.  The wet stones and structures looked more vibrant and brighter. The city was built on a gentle slope. Upon first entering, we came across the church known as the Palaestra Terrace. This church is a large structure made of old stones, shaped like a rectangle and featuring a total of four iron gates. There are two gates on the front of the building, and historical stone ruins have been placed in front of the gates. 

>Kentte benekli taşlarda özenle döşenmiş çokta geniş olmayan  uzun bir yoldan giriş yapılıyor. Kenti gezmek için muhtemelen ücret alıyorlar ama gişe bölümünde kimse olmadığı için direk içeri girdik. Kente geldiğimizde yağmur da şiddetini artırmıştı. Ama bu yağmur ve toprak kokusu gezimize ayrı bir güzellik katmıştı.  Sanki kenttin içinde doğa uyanmıştı.  Islanan taşlar ve yapılar daha canlı ve daha parlak görünüyordu. Kent hafif yamaca doğru kurulmuştu. İlk girişte Palaestra Terası adı verilen Kilise ile karşılaştık. Bu Kilise dikdörtgen şeklinde yapılmış toplamda dört demir kapısı olan büyük eski taşlardan yapılmış bir yapı görünümdedir. Yapının ön tarafında iki kapı ve kapının önünde de tarihi kalıntı taşlar koyulmuş. 


![IMG20260325175157.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTPQMbaSsa8u9gUxFafo1nXBZz92RGknza6mEPDJ2f8uF/IMG20260325175157.jpg)


![IMG20260325172733.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWkuYkZaDAnF7r8dCx8GpLDEBCe3qgm3QWc6rUe8kdaiq/IMG20260325172733.jpg)


![IMG20260325172823.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQpwjvMwM8iPGgiFWu6CKdbP3erf7XLiiqrpCe5rf7sj3/IMG20260325172823.jpg)

![IMG20260325173039.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQi5qs2wo3BXKNF9d2J2Kw7ZgE43NzCCreY5Mc6X7rCv5/IMG20260325173039.jpg)

![IMG20260325173329.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSoQMnsHSBfBYN1pCmDNjn8rx5sABTH9Vusp5WKVR2hPD/IMG20260325173329.jpg)

![IMG20260325172912.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRaNdBvP1uY42bbY1TUvaYGHGCsoC852G29bhAQ4WqgZb/IMG20260325172912.jpg)

![IMG20260325172909.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQme11b4a6eUJYkoXPYa88eyJMdS8xomjBxaHBbyJyEygph/IMG20260325172909.jpg)

When we entered through the open iron gates of the church, which has four walls, we saw round stone structures standing on the ground to the right and left of the building. The motifs on the stone blocks resembled the cross symbols of the Christian era. The slight widening of the cross’s arms is a style frequently seen in the Byzantine period.  The geometric shapes surrounding them—including triangles and squares—likely represent decorations imbued with both aesthetic and protective meanings.  Symbols drawn on stone blocks like these are commonly found on church buildings and gravestones. The symbols and styles on the stones, now wet from the rain, have become more distinct and clearer.

>Dört duvarı olan Kilisenin açık olan demir kapılarından içeri girdiğimizde, binanın sağ ve sol tarafında yerde duran yuvarlak taşlı yapıların olduğunu gördük.  Taş blokların üzerinde yer alan motifler, hristiyanlık dönemine ait olan haç işaretlerine benziyorduu.  Haçın uçlarının hafif genişlemesi  Bizans dönemlerinde de sıkça görülen stiller arasındadır.  Etrafındaki geometrik şekiller bunlar arasında üçgenler ve kareler de var  muhtemelen hem estetik hem de koruyucu anlamlar yüklenen süslemeleri ifade ediyor.  Buna benzer taş blokların üzerine çizilen semboller genelde kilise yapılarında ve mezar taşlarında çokça görülüyor. Yağmurla birlikte ıslanan taşların üzerindeki sembol ve stiller daha belirgin ve daha net ortaya çıkmış.


![IMG20260325173359.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPCbXxD81eN7LHx9gLs9evjKPKyu4UVteVqKEWSNrEQhs/IMG20260325173359.jpg)


![IMG20260325173423.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma8Dy61bXVSyD2ayavkLMSXTRkP63gy6gQPoXubmRDQe1/IMG20260325173423.jpg)


![IMG20260325173438.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCRdVVduNVJyCK5eKQMHfuxZ65JePBk5QUxY5WGv7Qhq/IMG20260325173438.jpg)

![IMG20260325173409.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaZMnQYRvw6hs1noTti348m6b3MGnL6m2g62CwGYnhDsr/IMG20260325173409.jpg)


![IMG20260325173703.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQbuvwtW5ao85zqAAiDyuuP1LFtKV61Vhm6qdgxx8xWFK/IMG20260325173703.jpg)

The church consists of two identical rooms. The hall of the other room is so seamlessly integrated with nature that grasses and flowers have sprouted from between the stones and walls, establishing their own independent presence. This room is more sheltered than the other and features an area paved with closely set stones. There are hidden passages in the room with the three arched stone openings that provide access to the other rooms. Stone blocks and historical remains can be found on the floor. Similarly, daisies and grasses struggling to emerge from the ground have also sprouted from between the walls. 

>Kilise iki aynı odadan oluşuyor. Diğer odanın salonu doğa ile o kadar bütünleşmiş ki, otlar çiçekler taşların ve duvarların arasından çıkarak kendi bağımsızlıklarını kurmuşlar.  Bu oda diğerine göre daha korunaklı ve sık taşlarını döşendiği bir alanlan oluşuyor. Kapalı üç kemer taşın bulunduğu odadan diğer odalara geçiş imkanını sağlayan gizli bölümlerde var. Yerlerde yine taş bloklar tarihi kalıntılar bulunuyor. Aynı şekilde toprağın üstünde yeni yeni çıkmaya çalışan papatya çiçekleri ve otlar da duvarların arasından fırlamışlar. 


![IMG20260325175016.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWdudvWv4hkHetSELd6E8bTVboHqaWseE982hvtiCugWb/IMG20260325175016.jpg)


![IMG20260325175204.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT5HzmvqiHXBmUS2US3v4Se4fK9aWcUPy5AW3tis634ks/IMG20260325175204.jpg)


![IMG20260325174955.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfPY5eYupDwtNF96MT5wX4HnJCnSAnN23ZoUH5Gedi39u/IMG20260325174955.jpg)


![IMG20260325174924.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQxTo2VUZy6oS6tTyqyygZbfTU1VtfrbsM11egALxa1Qn/IMG20260325174924.jpg)


![IMG20260325174938.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQufHLNUAuR1Ax6CZbrihj8v7o4mBvTK5KJhrvwmWzJEC/IMG20260325174938.jpg)

We can see several structures surrounding the church. While the damaged buildings struggle to remain standing, the historical ruins scattered across the grass and the symbols on them bring the traces of the past to light.  As you walk between the stone walls, you feel as though time has paused here to rest. The small flowers and grasses sprouting atop the walls look so beautiful in the rain that we bear witness to moments where nature and history converge. 

>Kilisenin etrafından birkaç yapının olduğunu görüyoruz. Hasar gören yapılar ayakta durmaya çalışırken, çimenlerin üzerinde yer alan tarihi kalıntılar ve bu kalıntıların üzerindeki semboller geçmişin izlerini gün yüzüne çıkarıyor.  Taş duvarların arasında yürürken zamanın burada durup dinlendiğini hissediyorsunuz.  Duvarların üstünde küçük küçük filizlenen çiçekler ve otlar yağmurla birlikte o kadar güzel görünüyor ki; doğa ile tarihin birleştiği anlara tanıklık ediyoruz. 


![IMG20260325174213.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNmAXMeus5A63vCc4r9aC3irxoKfB35hjw1cfMRim2mqD/IMG20260325174213.jpg)


![IMG20260325174216.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWPPdP56UUT2hD4FMwxdH5zxtJoAyEC8nKRiS5junSVeB/IMG20260325174216.jpg)


![IMG20260325174225.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQs4b9BjwiJjqEuMz8YYB3x24UsWpycBivFoTT8K3fXuq/IMG20260325174225.jpg)


![IMG20260325174457.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRSzKsjThZnJhDyUZDpWiQJB8AxWesD1xe5xTKYWWgkAU/IMG20260325174457.jpg)


![IMG20260325174623.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeAcXcVicASsPqsTKwc9ghFCCoSTMqf6Pgz7fY4mJHRa5/IMG20260325174623.jpg)


![IMG20260325174406.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVMZ1Mmj6CaWK3VPX9GVKLhQSkyFvUcUguxjaeYN7C8kJ/IMG20260325174406.jpg)

The gray sky and the fine rain falling gently over the city seemed to bring out its essence, its character, and its radiance even more. As I wandered through the city, the historic ruins and buildings around me seemed to come to life, carrying whispers of the past into the present and telling me a different story with every step. The weariness of the clouds and their gray hues seemed to lend the city an extra atmosphere. The raindrops falling on the buildings added a melancholic air to the historical ruins. 

>Gökyüzünün gri oluşu ve yağmur damlalarının ince ince kentin üzerine yağması kentin içini , duruşunu ve parlaklığını sanki daha da ortaya çıkarıyordu. Kentin içinde gezerken, etraftaki tarihi kalıntılar ve yapılar sanki canlanmış ve geçmişin fısıltılarını bugüne taşıyarak her adımda bana başka bir hikaye anlatıyordu. Bulutların yorgunluğu ve gri tonları kentte ekstra bir hava katmış gibi görünüyordu.  Yapıların üzerine düşen yağmur damlaları tarihi kalıntılara melankolik bir hava katmış. 


![IMG20260325173336.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYnKQJThqev53eWJuURSviWnjmY4TeBc9v7nJ8LCpZ4Nr/IMG20260325173336.jpg)


![IMG20260325173640.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVfCnXwmkYH5eHSTMSqLdjnpNCBx1gZAgjamswfQ9K99F/IMG20260325173640.jpg)



![IMG20260325173109.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWZKqdpkn3UfphEMBNmoJqR4jiR5PHof4bXGB6EiF42dy/IMG20260325173109.jpg)


![IMG20260325173201.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTYNVHa1r9yxwgBqvhanqrqH7Pj4mD2ZvYh2ZRLjqqJ9H/IMG20260325173201.jpg)


![IMG20260325173244.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTn6GQLrP3cx4q9ya5SEjc8BG3BK6TPucSpMPA6NCXB9y/IMG20260325173244.jpg)

One of the most impressive features of the ancient city of Kaunos—and the one I was most curious about—is the city’s theater. You enter the ancient theater through a large arched gateway built into the high wall.  Once you step through the gate, you climb the stone steps to see the magnificent theater stage.  At the entrance, information panels on the side walls explain the paintings, historical artifacts, and symbols from that era. 

>Kaunos Antik Kentin en etkileyici ve benim en çok merak ettiğim şekillerinden biri de kentin tiyatrosudur. Antik Tiyatroya yüksek duvarda oluşturulan büyük bir kemerli kapıdan giriliyor.  Kapıdan içeri gidiğinizde taşlı merdivenleri çıkarak o muhteşem tiyatro sahnesini görüyorsunuz.  Girişte yan duvarlarda o dönemlere ait resimleri, tarihi kalıntıları ve sembolleri açıklayan bilgi panoları yer alıyor. 


![IMG20260325174308.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR7RWW4ZgnzNVzLiUiHQnYrwpkZs6NWnt1ziShP7QK4L2/IMG20260325174308.jpg)

![IMG20260325173804.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQme83PD3uuCtoMoz6KsaKH8njWbW2d5xA6QKUYHfhwr6uT/IMG20260325173804.jpg)

![IMG20260325174009.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSTTNFo3Gi82BfaXNX7V8R8rmtybnPiWSwtrY5xqZLCiz/IMG20260325174009.jpg)

The first thing that caught my eye when I saw the theater was the daisy flowers adorning the spaces between the semi-circular seating tiers. They were so beautifully arranged between the tiers that they seemed to have become one with the history of the past. This semi-circular theater layout is found in most ancient cities in Turkey. This layout generally reflects the architectural influences of the Hellenistic and Roman periods. It was likely designed to allow the audience to see the stage more comfortably. Here, the green grass and flowers sprouting from between the stones and steps, along with the olive tree rising in the center, have infused the structure with a completely different spirit.  It’s as if they’ve become the indispensable spectators of the plays performed here over the centuries. 


>Tiyatroyu gördüğüm de ilk dikkat çeken şey yarim daire şeklinde yükselen oturma basamaklarının aralarını süsleyen papatya çiçekleri oldu.  Oturma basamaklarının aralarına o kadar güzel yerleşmişler ki;  sanki geçmiş tarihle  bir bütün haline gelmişler.  Bu yarim daire şeklindeki tiyatro düzeni Türkiye'de bulunan çoğu antik kentte yer alıyor. Bu düzen genelde Helenistik ve Roma Döneminin mimari yansımalarını işaret ediyor. Bu düzen muhtemelen seyircilerin sahneyi daha rahat görebilmesi için yapılmış. Burada taşların ve basamakların arasından çıkan yeşil otlar ve çiçeklerle ortada yükselen zeytin ağacı, yapıya bambaşka bir ruh katmış.  Sanki yüzyılar boyunca sahnelenen oyunların vazgeçilmez seyircileri haline gelmişler. 


![IMG20260325173901.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSb9SiGTCXLUmJThRD5qPtBpv6CCJTdikGS4TVeBdPoao/IMG20260325173901.jpg)


![IMG20260325173906.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmarwYPZdUXFz1kFkfKjqEyn2jPDDCYcmg8gNebK5ArjXM/IMG20260325173906.jpg)


![IMG20260325173909.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX2hFSujVadVhCnjb2WXXRXx1JDKe32VZPA2eET2azMR5/IMG20260325173909.jpg)

The theater is situated in a truly beautiful location. It is built on a natural slope, perched at a vantage point overlooking the landscape. Entry is through arched doorways formed in certain sections of the seating steps. Although the stage has suffered damage, the beauty of nature has obscured this ruin. 

>Tiyatronun konumu oldukça güzel ayarlanmış. Tiyatro doğal bir yamaca yaslanmış manzaraya hakim bir noktaya kurulmuş.  Oturma basamaklarının belirli bölümlerinde kemer şeklinde oluşturulan kapılardan giriş yapılıyor. Sahne her ne kadar hasar görmüş olsada doğanın güzelliği bir bu çöküntünün üzerini kapatmış. 


![IMG20260325173912.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPQJk45p2ghZ9q79gwspnryqwwuYx179FcvKn3er2uwsk/IMG20260325173912.jpg)


![IMG20260325173924.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeVQp3QaonPa8RtfqNxPj3e33UgyKN4AtDaFwRJ2SuyaZ/IMG20260325173924.jpg)


![IMG20260325173930.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV8M4xW5hZfuPtBnHhUP2QtUDpg1GgeDbZg4Zwfnvcs9R/IMG20260325173930.jpg)

The ancient city of Kaunos was very different from any other ancient city I’ve visited so far. The theater area, in particular, truly captivated me. Because this city wasn’t isolated. The beauty of nature—the trees, flowers, and grasses—had clung tightly to it, become one with it, and seemed to be an integral part of its spirit and its past.  

>Kaunos Antik Kent,şimdiki kadar gezdiğim antik kentlerden çok farklıydı. Özellikle tiyatro alanı beni gerçekten çok büyüledi. Çünkü bu kent yalnız değildi. Doğanın güzellikleri ağaçları, çiçekleri ve otları, ona sımsıkı tutunmuş, onunla bütünleşmiş ve adeta ruhunun ve geçmişin bir parçası olmuştu.  


![Passenger777.gif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRJC4twuaVWbv36cmAFG8Gc1LTcYxXa4qaoW3kqzgJRx8/Passenger777.gif)

My recent trip to Italy didn't exactly start well. Here's my bad and good expectations of Naples, Italy. ![1000054180.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/243zbSMR1yHGHZPQD9KqKVdJK8s5Nv3NG8bZZAu8XssE69SDVgKCMM8p1CKwHtuENACeW.jpg) Ten minutes after we were due to land, the captain announced that due to thunderstorms, he had tried, but was unable to land in Naples. We were now on our way to Rome, some 250km away. An hour later we arrived at Rome. They were figuring out what to do next. The options were to either take us by bus, or fly back to Naples. If we still couldn't land in Naples because of the thunderstorm, we had to fly back to Rome and by that time, we may not be able to land in Rome due to the night time curfew. It was already 11pm and we were kept on board. People were getting very agitated especially when we found out other planes landed Naples when we couldn't. The captain blamed it on lightning which happens very quick. He was essentially closing the door for potential compensation claims. ![1000054198.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23vi25jAxteA6XKdChPMExnHsoBqs8QjpK2ofaKF3Rt3vStADhDT3mYnttxjdg6Lf1JTT.jpg) Eventually they decided on the first option - bus. By the time we passed border control, it was past midnight. A handful of us had to wait for our luggage, and that took another two hours. We have no idea what was happening and the ground staff couldn't give us an answer. I'm sure it would be much quicker to go out to the plane and get it ourselves!!!. But everyone was so tired and hungry. Luckily there was a vending machine and I managed to grab a few sandwiches. By the time we left at 2am, thid vending machine was totally empty. ![1000054197.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EokWr51nS1NewCC2WC471d2uuT9LJwsDHZpoZ7hsAmtKYAGGJW2P3VcZY2xZVbvDeMA.jpg) Finally, we got on the bus and arrived at Naples airport at 5am!!! What an eventful way to start our holiday --- ### Deep fried pizza After a few hours sleep it was time to get some proper food. Naples is the birthplace of pizza, we have to start with that, but not the traditional pizza as we know. We went for a fried pizza, which was delicious. Or maybe we were still recovering from last night's ordeal.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EonkRgMd9aczFPsyjR4BLK49BQU52jZwyhowxh3yE8VJSQs4MVy29VEU86j48bULJNR.jpg
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23wMabRi3nwwtED64XYVgndYQCvvi5WmuT681VeMiKeDCuU9gGgSQTUtbBvLUWp6gp5jh.jpg https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23z7NW7o3FMNPhBsLugef8JkZKK4vFWaFJbqBmNPeeXWn8Za68jN37EtAa9vjzEbtTZ8E.jpg
--- ### Maradona Naples is also famous for Maradona. He's treated like god here, or is the city milking his connection? There's a fine line. You can see his murals everywhere, and they even have a special shrine for him at Quartieri Spagnoli. It's a little trek, and after all the effort to get there I made sure to leave a Worldmappin Hive pin behind.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpzygSNTTNYcg21gctgaeWCkC9yCC9Jvmx6tztLGVd9Ho9j8MPch7Wv7VJCfFy7RvK9.jpg
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/Ep3duNTLger7ACfbdvzV5rJfmc4Lk9NE2zUASAxtCigjG35ZD9Re68p7J1wd3ZjQrCX.jpg
![1000054372.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23xVEbg8QNhkxEoSMBtskaPbC5e8Vw4ebc3w3yYYSQYW1We5v4kJB1MwCJjHBEXgTPJnj.jpg) During our stay, we visited some typical touristy spots, and went for a [grand afternoon tea](https://peakd.com/hive-152524/@livinguktaiwan/the-gran-caffe-gambrinus-in-naples-and-all-the-queues). |We wandered around the alleyways in the old town |kept on drifting back to the jaw dropping Galleria Umberto I | |-|-| |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EoEpY14vS4PaT4aWXTcRvvo8csWQKtCwRcd1udusiuoRWY3TKC9b628VUk188hYJ5u4.jpg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EogLLgzEJJqkLvXD9iZcPuNHLvUcerxy2a7dFnBkNnGwbghStsbRzLe4718cCYPdaug.jpg| |strolled along the seafront looking out to Sorrento and Capri|and when I was tired, took solace in the Basilica| |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EqhNNBqQdXVhJXJQmcDk5GkQL3CfaBnkhYpJs6ZwY2ryxtAKCHRnmz9hTpg8oh2NcNm.jpg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpGQJkpCGEE7wu9vQRdBs21ig4doAsYaeA5J5JQiwDvtoJeo2AwbrkWq7GRX1tfuWD7.jpg| My eyes wandered up to the dome as I was resting inside the basilica. And it really bugged me. I get 7, 7 days in a week? But why 32? Where does 32 fit in our life? Is this supposed to make us think about the greater universe? Can anyone enlighten me please? ### Napoli Sotterranea One of the must go, in my opinion is the Napoli Sotterranea, but only if you're not claustrophobic. And if you do go, make sure to [book in advance](https://www.napolisotterranea.org/en/). ![1000054712.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EoeDyDU3xNcoadrLHDevWmRBr8NH1QScVqHdtRiF5QoWebBUGa3GRW1nKeS8BCmuHG1.jpg) Naples has an impressive underground network dating back to 300BC. The Greeks mined the volcanic sandstone called tuff because it was strong and durable, and used it to build their temples. Then the Romans dug tunnels and aqueduct to feed water to different parts of the city. And in more recent times, the underground network was used as air raid shelters during the war. And this is what's so fascinating about the tour as we're led 40m underground and walk through 2400 years of history. We walked through dark narrow conduits were only a person could just about pass through. This lead us to massive cisterns with water as clear as crystal. Ending up in chambers big enough for tens of people. I had no expectation of the tour. But fair to say, it exceeded all my expectations. Highly recommended!

Hello everyone, I hope you are doing great and have a nice spring days. In the previous post, I wrote about my last trip to Lasko, Slovenia, so in the coming days I will share some more impressive spots of this place. 
This was not my first visit to Lasko, but it was my first visit to the historical sites on the hills above this place. Every time we were there we looked at the imposing church with two domes high in the hills from the foot of the town.

![IMG_20251110_110608.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eqd6bDeC8x8cVuRu6hLezHjkvxih6YymexiwMPxp7MvejgxNcxwmbiUWTMQ4CEe5hwx.jpg)

It was the Shmichel (Šmihel) church, we learned from the locals. It is a 17th-century building constructed in the Baroque style.

![IMG_20251110_110803.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoiVi6rsT28pUXwn67znQRwNwGxxkD2VYu4mqRmn9DZWJxgwTcskJYax6PW5i9DhxFG.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQyiLZBidoDNRJyird1Wx4ALqMu7fySRoRSqyfJLTpewb2oKCiqCNT4hPa8akyBPBk.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqUfqeQBXZE5ibjXYdf77i71bH6SYuZ17QTw8rv9ySe4DspMmyRTGyabkDfVb3Sn2b6.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EorysDb32VqJiADCFxshBP33AaQFw6EAJGEpZVfAESe6WgPUQh8Ch3pqGYGAjR5aejJ.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110835.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJZYyECY2oVMGCzEyh2BvDUVH9BZxatpkFyF8Uo16qER32vN2MHJxPj8CkeQh7f5hw.jpg)

Our visit to Shmihel (St Michael) Church in Laško started with a simple moment of curiosity. From the distance, it looked peaceful and inviting, almost like it was calling us to come closer and that was enough to make us want to climb up and see it for ourselves.

![IMG_20251110_111429.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep7mxYshSwtgmq9HZ4dvwaB6Qpdb5oThen8d5hwtDbpwg7oYBtDD3pe1NKFwM49xpoz.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110923.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EowECQNSqTb1hSMr3uxDTq8zvVvXndhsH8cELKasmX3GHm6AUbeGz1CfoPBKYebYK17.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110946.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqBZHjA2b2nYpQrXxPWXkciv1pq7RfBAtUr333dpJRC8dZhgbYzz6YdL6drHCp54eFo.jpg)

The walk toward the church felt like a small adventure. As we got closer, we noticed a statue standing in front of the entrance, watching over the surroundings.

![IMG_20251110_110622.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqaycN4sgZWkgW2SD9NLxtiCdMaV7wA9GbWWcZNHfjVRayXSg9VTcUXsGWUNozcKDEa.jpg)

It added a special character to the place, giving it a sense of history and quiet significance. 

![IMG_20251110_111426.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqSTczga2BcwNPYXNyUYnDD9RDkQsNpGBTZmW8uz3P3gJdV2LwD91BSAzciEES1zAMb.jpg)

The nature around was fascinating.

![IMG_20251110_110706.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EnqQiXUx8uYfaexb5WLZkXwoVDfVDSm6T4n42rYAyjNknJJbTHkpbR4MFAGSnuBY2Qg.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110644.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqL5q1rZvLaDSESYF9JUWo2CyLCTz8pdgASCYKu3hwqZb3xbEhadWMRuhMTdw5kytbM.jpg)

I enjoyed looking into the distance, high and far, breathing in the fresh clean air.

![IMG_20251110_112657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoTZVXC4UKPPMteHVco1PWbPXmqMmA6xi69nF1fz2oUtpG4vK9XvwJhYMpPNzsjKUkz.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_113528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoTbrvVZA2yXrCeM2BcZK9JnMFPcdNPMzWmXLy31QTvhfSLXJ9S5ptCBZSXtLrweSSo.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_113435.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqSU2bG2YmrUhdmiiC47DUC8AmAJbLZntBtFGmUGV5DMZHLStzh9Rj88xYxHe6SxetR.jpg)

Unfortunately, we didn't get the chance to see the inside of the church. The doors were locked, so we could only catch a glimpse through the keyhole. Even that tiny view sparked our imagination just enough to wonder what the full interior might look like.

![IMG_20251110_111052.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJW8wqp7qcdpzzzv3ovbfzqY9s5goSjUREbK968yGjmXnkENwpzCdgX4HSZK5hq9zh.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111100.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCfdg9TFmbsy3D5xgc4toB7UeK4dQxtT9KAzVRgdQE9CeK7nBnTP3rHiV2bf52V9af.jpg)

Still, the visit didn't feel incomplete. Standing there, surrounded by nature and silence, with the town below and the hills around us, was more than enough. 

![IMG_20251110_111600.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpNpQ52fvQb8Cj1n7DAo63B3XQPaDw2PZc8CRxEeDqFLxtbbpujedx7ebNeEs4Kq6m9.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqNDJncQbmsnrRG8Z8mpNjwpw2vjL3rP9K9bLa9bsyyvuptMxQsAErQv5NqG2WJjt4A.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111609.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eokd7HJbSn9Vex513S9aNYm79nQKqzyVPuP65hTUfqKZ6ip2Yn6AVi6czH5kPSa8WVn.jpg)

Sometimes, it's not about seeing everything, but about the feeling a place leaves behind and Šmihel Church certainly left one worth remembering.

![IMG_20251110_111528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eqd72ZRWwdcPhEhMCk9fyJeP5Cdmm8rfNK1sBcB1JB1oAwfCPzHMWUGYoJGttxUTaVB.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111650.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqSUbUFB1UqvQ2oTJDJuK5dPcLEpCk4Px1NCibfA1B6FwnLc9niWPLqJfCqRVGVKh92.jpg)

My kids are also happier wandering around, as if that air gave them some extra energy. We felt strong and healthy there. The locals told us that there is another church nearby, so then we headed there...

![IMG_20251110_111727.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eoc75w1UyYuRGuJprKhU3A6WEvLvZZ6Uuwni1GJSHep5XarEsjYHA4mTqzWCjJexjk6.jpg)

![4i88GgaV8qiFkxbnGCXnHPUK3daVLCQA4oDc4iy6ghu2vJQJmmeoVEo8rvajHaCCkUyqJATNCMc48vtE83mAWqDQJEkMdBPfjJVFfd4oyRFTSogDiDskgQcJut.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGvUz9hKnnCbtpUM2j1FJdAutJrrz3gZ4rmwugVpGJkqiKwUMv715DrsSZo7inCi8x.webp)

Thank you for reading. 

Jelena

I recall many years ago and playing NCAA College Football on I think it was the Playstation and kind of being in awe about how the people who had made that game had the real rosters of every single college football team, including pictures of most of their faces and this really made the game seem a lot more lifelike even if the graphics were a bit dated.   

I wondered at the time how this was even possible because I had heard stories about how athletes get paid a silly amount of money for advertisements that they were in so how on earth could any game possible afford to pay what would have been around 100,000 people to use their likeness in a game?

<center> https://i.redd.it/96j5hkd16rf81.png
[src](https://i.redd.it/96j5hkd16rf81.png)
<sub> That's quite the blowout! </sub> </center>

Well as it turns out two thing were true:  1, the players weren't being compensated in any way, and 2, it was a lot more complicated than what I thought.

The rule has always been that athletics in universities in the United States were at that time, something that the young people could not be compensated for in any way other than receiving their tuition and room and board given for free.  There was not to be any other sort of incentive for the players.   Obviously some of the colleges cheated on this and rewarded the best players with certain perks and I'm sure that just like in the movie *Blue Chips* - which is a great film that you should check out - there were some shady deals involving envelopes filled with cash being distributed as well.

College Football and Basketball in particular are huge moneymakers and for most of my life the people that were playing it were not compensated for their work at all.  Well, other than getting a degree in whatever they want without really needing to work for it and the ability to go pro for big bucks.  

I don't know exactly when it happened because I guess I wasn't really paying attention but in the recent past this all changed.  Now student athletes are able to be compensated for NIL (name, image, and likeness) in all manner of things and this includes in video games but extends well beyond that. These days the top players likely have agents and scouts that are shopping for sponsorship and raking in millions of dollars for teenage boys (and some girls I guess) for all manner of things.

Considering the amount of money involved in the larger universities' teams, this would be a very easy system to be exploited.   While the universities themselves cannot compensate players, their "boosters" or other organizations with loose ties to the university wouldn't have any trouble organizing said sponsors to the point where it is basically the same thing as going into a price war for a salary.   

There are plenty of people complaining about this already that are on the boards of the smaller or less well-known universities who are making claims that the larger and better established universities are going to end up creating dynasties that cannot be dethroned because the athletes who go there are guaranteed very large NIL payouts even though this information will not be written on any contract because it is illegal to offer it.   There are a lot of things that can be conveyed without a piece of paper to back it up though.  

<center> https://voltedu.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/2025-NIL-Top-10-Highest-Paid-College-Athletes-590x340.png
[src](https://voltedu.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/2025-NIL-Top-10-Highest-Paid-College-Athletes-590x340.png)</center>

We are already seeing some college athletes that are getting paid salaries that would make many of their professional counterparts a bit jealous.   You no doubt recognize all of the college logos up there if you are a US sport fan, because they are all some of the most well-known sport universities.   

I agree, that this creates a sort of unofficial "big boy club" that the smaller colleges would struggle to participate in or to just straight up find it impossible to compete with.   

This can end up being a bad thing because even though it is kind of like that anyway, we will likely start to see the same 12 teams or so always perform a lot better than the other several thousand teams that are out there.  

There has already been talk about adjusting the NIL system, a kind of nipping it in the bud before places get used to it and I don't have any idea how it is going to pan out.  I mean, if the richest teams ended up having the most success in college football and basketball, that's just kind of a reflection of what the real world of sports is all about anyway and it probably cannot be prevented.   They will find a way around it and they likely always have.  There are "booster clubs" for basically all university athletic programs and while I don't have any first-hand knowledge, I would imagine that the sole purpose of these organizations is to corrupt the system as much as possible.  

But the people who are saying that payment to college athletes should be illegal I kind of think that they have a point.   There are some seriously wealthy athletic programs in existence out there and the smaller schools have zero chance of being able to compete with that.  

I read a little bit about the President of the US making some sort of executive order to change this, but just like anything that guy does, it will probably be fought in court just because of who he is. 

In the end I think that college sports are a lot more exciting that pro sports or at least, they were.   If it becomes a question of whoever has the most money wins, it kind of loses a lot of its allure.
